predecessors.name: Kara-Khanid Khanate
predecessors.text: the Western Khanate in Transoxiana, 'making Samarkand the capital'

successors.name: Khwarazmian Empire
successors.text: Samarkand and Transoxiana: Muhammad II 'executed Uthman ... and finally extinguished the Western Karakhanid state' in 1212

ledger.x: 1046: the Western Khanate of the Kara-Khanids is formed at Samarkand.
1066: the Fergana valley passes from the Eastern to the Western Khanate.
1073: Malik-Shah drives the Kara-Khanids back and takes Termez.
1089: Seljuk rule is established over Transoxiana and the khans become vassals.
1137: Yelü Dashi defeats the Western Karakhanids at Khujand and takes the Fergana valley and Tashkent.
1210: the Khwarezm-Shah takes Samarkand after the Qara Khitai withdraw, allied to Uthman.
1212: Samarkand revolts against the Khwarezmians; Muhammad retakes it.
1212: the Western Karakhanid state is extinguished.

wars.name: Seljuk campaigns in Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory: Termez taken in 1073; Samarkand and Bukhara taken in 1087; 'the entire Turkistan Region, up to the borders of China, was brought under Seljuk rule in 1089', the khans kept as vassals.

wars.name: Qara Khitai conquest of the Fergana valley (Khujand)
wars.outcome: Qara Khitai victory near Khujand in May 1137; the Fergana valley and Tashkent oasis pass to the Qara Khitai.

wars.name: Battle of Qatwan
wars.outcome: Qara Khitai victory on 9 September 1141 on the Qatwan steppe north of Samarkand; Samarkand's khanate and Khwarazm become Qara Khitai vassals, Yelü Dashi appointing Mahmud's brother Ibrahim at Samarkand.

wars.name: Khwarazmian conquest of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Bukhara taken in 1207, Samarkand in 1210; the revolt of Samarkand in 1212 ends in Uthman's execution and the end of the Western Karakhanid state.

certainty.note: Oasis and steppe frontiers throughout, no survey or treaty line; the Oxus was the line with the Ghaznavids and then the Seljuks ('The Oxus River thus became the boundary'), the Fergana-Zhetysu border with the Eastern Khanate was…
